title: Family PACE plan
summary: Primary, Alternate, Contingency, Emergency: four ways to reach each other in order, with an example for this household.

sources.title: CISA: Leveraging the PACE Plan into the Emergency Communications Ecosystem
CISA SAFECOM/NCSWIC: Leveraging the PACE Plan (PDF)

blocks.text: A **PACE plan** names four ways to reach each other, in order, so everyone knows what to try when the first one fails. The letters stand for **Primary, Alternate, Contingency, Emergency**. Government agencies use it. Here is how to use it for a family.

blocks.alt: Four stacked boxes for a family PACE plan. P, Primary: cell phone call. A, Alternate: text message. C, Contingency: Meshtastic text. E, Emergency: FRS or GMRS radio at the meeting point. Move down a level when the one above fails.
blocks.caption: Move down a level when the one above fails.

items: **Primary:** your normal, everyday way of getting in touch.
**Contingency:** used if both Primary and Alternate have failed.
**Emergency:** the fourth level, for when everything else is not working.

blocks.text: You move from one level to the next when the current one fails.

CISA says a method that depends on the same path as an earlier level has no value. Its example: listing email, Facebook and texting as three levels is useless if all three depend on the same cellular data. It also says a plan may need an **outside contact**, a place or person outside the affected area.

rows: Texts and calls both use the cell network, so if the whole network is down, skip straight to Contingency.
Your private channel; set up in advance.
FRS or GMRS radio at the meeting point
Go to the meeting point and use the family channel.

blocks.text: Add a **check-in schedule** you can keep, such as a set time each hour, and an **out-of-area contact** each person can call or text. Write down code words and meeting places too. The Comms screen has places for all of this under **Comms - Our plan**.

items: Write it down and give everyone a copy. Keep the plan simple.
Practice. CISA says organizations should practice a PACE plan during training and exercises so everyone can carry it out. Test each level before you need it, including Meshtastic and the radios.
Each person should be comfortable with the backup methods before the main one fails.
Everyone knows the four levels in order
Each level uses a different path (not all on the cell network)
Meshtastic radios set up and tested (see the Meshtastic guides)
FRS/GMRS channel chosen and meeting point agreed
Check-in times and an out-of-area contact written down
Plan entered on the Comms screen and shared with family
